subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw accept `append?: boolean` on the existing `write` tool as the permanent append contract for ordinary agent, cron, and monitor workflows, or require a different append API before closing this issue?
rationale: The failure is source-reproducible, but the remaining fix is a public model-facing and extension-observable tool contract that automation should not approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept append on write
options.body: Land the open implementation after review, keeping overwrite as the default and using `append: true` for safe accumulation.

options.title: Choose a separate append contract
options.body: Ask for a replacement shape such as `mode: "append"` or a dedicated append tool before merging public API changes.

options.title: Defer the core API change
options.body: Keep this issue open and rely on backups or shell-redirect workarounds while accepting that ordinary write calls can still truncate shared files.

recommendation.title: Accept append on write
recommendation.body: Land the open implementation after review, keeping overwrite as the default and using `append: true` for safe accumulation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the shared write-tool API and Peter has the strongest current history on the shared agent tool-definition surface.
